reviews.author: Bungeoppang Boy (Bunggeoppang Boy)
reviews.text:
It is close to Apgujeong Station on Line 3. Located about 5-10 minutes away. Jackson Pizza is an American-style pizza restaurant that first opened in eastern Hannam in 2015, and has since expanded its chain to various regions. The Apgujeong branch is a take-out restaurant, and a 10% discount on the existing price is available for take-out.

It takes about 15-20 minutes after ordering. This was my second visit, and this day I ordered Hawaiian pizza. There are three sizes: P, M, and L. It may seem like a small amount, but when you eat them all, size M is a bit large for an adult male. On my previous visit, I had Delight Pepperoni and Super Jackson and was satisfied with the taste and quantity. I also tried the Hawaiian pizza and it was good because the pineapple was emphasized and it wasn't too sweet.

When ordering 1 plate, cola is not included and 1 special sauce is included in the price. The coleslaw salad, a side dish I ordered, was not too strong and went well with the salty pizza. I was able to enjoy the pizza, considering that its texture and taste change significantly when it cools down, but people who don't like salty American pizza might find the pizza a little salty.

Prices vary depending on the size and taste of the pizza. L size is around 30,000 won, M size is between 10,000 and 20,000 won, and P size is around 10,000 won. It may feel a little expensive, but considering the rise in prices and the location of Apgujeong, it was not bad. I intend to visit again next time

reviews.author: ethan ghymn
reviews.text:
For dinner, each young family member is asked to bring their favorite pepperoni pizza and BHC sprinkle chicken.

If I wanted American pizza, I would have gone to PIZZA PIZZA in Yeoksam-dong, which is my favorite pizza place these days, but I saved it because I was curious and wanted to go there after passing by. It's close to my house, and I decided to stop by Jackson Pizza, which I heard about in a recent review as having American pizza.

I parked nearby and entered the store. The interior was decorated to have a retro feel or an American In-N-Out Burger feel. When I entered, there were only a few customers, but by the time the pizza I ordered came out, it was full of customers.

I was already going to order half and half, so when I looked at the menu, half and half was only available when ordering in large size, and the large size didn't feel that big, so I had no choice but to order the large size, but I would like pepperoni and Hawaiian.

There is a price difference between pepperoni and Hawaiian, so I thought that half and half would match the price of the expensive pizza like in a typical chicken restaurant, but fortunately, that was not the case and the price was somewhere between the more expensive pizza and the less expensive pizza.

The cashier asked if I wanted to order jalapenos and pickles, which are billed separately, and I said it was okay since I didn't eat them before.

When I looked at the back, I saw crushed red pepper, so I asked for it because I liked it. I thought it was strange because it felt like it wasn't being charged separately.

I was told it would take about 10 to 15 minutes, so I sat on a chair on one side of the store and waited.

There was a sealing fan spinning on the ceiling to create an American atmosphere, and various sodas and beers were displayed in a refrigerated showcase, so you could take them out and pay if you wanted them.

The pizza is baked in a common conveyor-type oven, and the clerk puts it in a pizza box and hands it to you in a wide plastic wrapper for easy taking home.

When I got home and unwrapped it, the pepperoni looked like a typical pepperoni, but the Hawaiian had plenty of pineapple, the Canadian bacon was relatively thickly sliced, and sprinkled with shredded basil, so it felt quite fresh.

Inside the plastic wrapper, there was a dipping sauce that looked like ranch sauce, which I liked as I like ranch sauce.

I tried the Hawaiian without touching the pepperoni for a young family. The sweetness of the pineapple and the fairly thick Canadian bacon were a good combination. The dough was not tough or floury and had a relatively light texture, so it was good. However, the tomato sauce was not particularly tasty.

The crust of the pizza felt relatively light, so it felt good to eat on its own, but it felt good when dipped in the ranch sauce that was added, but it felt somewhat sour and had a yogurt-like taste. When I asked the store later, they said it was not just ranch sauce, but horseradish ranch sauce.

I asked my young family member if I could eat pepperoni, and I was told that I could eat it. I tasted a slice and it tasted like the typical pepperoni pizza I like. As expected, I like that the dough is relatively light, but it's disappointing that the thickness of the pepperoni is thin.

The family said it was the most delicious Hawaiian pizza they had ever tasted.

Overall, I was passing by and was curious and wanted to go, so I saved it and stopped by because I heard it had an American pizza feel. These days, it feels like more and more American-style pizza places are popping up, and it felt good. However, it doesn't feel like it's particularly delicious, and it's not the menu of Korean pizza places that are difficult to understand these days, so it's closer to a good feeling. If I visit again, I think I'll try the deep dish pizza. Rather, if it's the American pizza that I like, I think I'll keep going to PIZZA PIZZA in Yeoksam-dong...

reviews.author: Seongwoo Kim
reviews.text:
Gentleman [Chikpiece]

⠀
I went to [Chik Peas] on Garosu-gil, which specializes in Mediterranean salads. The term ‘Mediterranean salad’ felt a little unfamiliar, but you can think of it as a salad that actively utilizes Middle Eastern foods such as falafel and hummus. Another characteristic is that it contains ingredients that are somewhat unfamiliar to salads, such as chickpeas, olives, and lamb. These days, the ‘Mediterranean diet’ is becoming a trend. The Mediterranean diet is a healthy diet that is registered as a UNESCO World Intangible Cultural Heritage, and refers to the unique eating habits of regions located along the Mediterranean coast, such as Greece, Spain, and Italy. It is characterized by a low-saturated fat and high dietary fiber diet centered on fruits, vegetables, grains, and nuts, and has recently been in the spotlight to the extent that it was selected as the ‘best diet of 2020.’
⠀
Garosu-gil [Chick Peas] is one of the few restaurants in Korea that serves Mediterranean food. They also sell vegan menus, and the healthy diet menus without the burden of calories seem to fit well with the commercial district of Garosu-gil. The high proportion of foreign guests and the colorful interior made me feel like I was in a foreign country, even if only for a moment. Food was self-service, where you ordered at the counter and received it yourself, and you could also take plates and sauces from one side as needed. You have to endure some inconvenience, but the price is reasonable. As for the cheap menu, it ranges from 6,000 won to 10,000 won, so I think it is an excellent price range in the commercial district of Garosu-gil.
⠀
On this day, I ordered three things: ‘Lamb Kebab Rice,’ ‘Scallion Salad,’ and ‘Original Hummus.’ I think ‘Original Hummus’ is the menu that best represents the store called [Chik Peas]. ‘Hummus’ is a kind of dipping sauce made by boiling chickpeas, and on top of it is ‘falafel’, which is made with ingredients such as chickpeas, parsley, cumin, and cilantro and fried into round shapes. Because it is a menu consisting only of vegetables, it is overall light and the hummus has a subtle savory flavor. Although it doesn't have an intuitive taste, it feels like you can eat it without any burden. Of course, there seem to be likes and dislikes. ‘Lamb Kebab Rice’ was a disappointing dish because the lamb was topped in the form of a hamburger steak, but the flavor was weak and the temperature was cold, while the ‘Fish Salad’ was okay because the steak was softer than expected.
⠀
As the domestic vegan population increases, restaurants that sell vegan menus, and even vegan restaurants that only sell menus for vegetarians, are gradually appearing. I think [Chick Peas] is one of the good options for those people, and I think it's a restaurant that even non-vegetarians can go and enjoy.

reviews.text: This is a place where you can taste American French course cuisine with a San Francisco feel. I made a reservation two weeks in advance and was able to be seated right away without waiting. Three people went and ordered three courses for 38,000 won, consisting of four dishes: entree + plat + deseert + boisson. There were three dishes each in the entree and plat, so I ordered all three dishes of each course because I wanted to try a variety of things. The aperitif bread came out first, and a little later, onion soup made with gratin with Gruyere cheese, blue d'Auvergne cheese and rattlesnake salad, and braised snails in a soft mushroom cream sauce were served. The rattoise salad was average, but the onion soup and snails were really delicious. For mains, I ordered pan braised chicken, homemade French-style gnocchi, and seafood dishes. The pan braised chicken and gnocchi were really delicious. The sorbet I chose for dessert was sweet and delicious, and the coffee wasn't that impressive, but it wasn't bad. For a course costing 38,000 won, it was a satisfying experience to be able to enjoy a French course meal at a reasonable price with a fairly generous menu.

#Sinsa-dong #Bubbet

“Stable Buvette”

The popularity of Bouvet, which made Seoul buzz in its early days, quickly collapsed due to problems with the quantity and taste of food, price, and service.
I said this in my first review, and after going a couple of times, I dismissed it as a restaurant I had no more expectations from...

Several years after opening, I visited Bouvet again because it was easy to make reservations, and I feel like it has established itself as a stable restaurant.

The service has also improved and is friendly and skilled.
Unlike the feeling of being confused about the food, the menus are comfortably stable.

In particular, French onion soup is of exceptional quality in Korea. Not only the taste, but the temperature I pointed out before is perfect.

Even the dry French toast was cooked gently and well.

The Carrot Lappé comes in just the right amount, so it's a great side dish for brunch, and the light taste of Bouvet is different from the recipes circulating on social media.

If this is a change, it would be nice to make Bouvet our family brunch restaurant.

I also came across this store through an advertisement on Instagram, and even though Philly cheesesteak isn't my favorite menu item, I remember visiting and trying Jim's Steaks South Street, one of the best Philly cheesesteak restaurants, when I traveled to Philadelphia, so I was glad to stop by.

I was disappointed to see that the Costco food court's bulgogi bake, which has a vaguely similar feel to it, replacing the salty taste of a Philly cheesesteak with a slightly sweet taste, doesn't seem to be on sale these days, but it's nice to see it.

They said there was no break time, so I stood in front of the store located in the alley next to Gentle Monster to have a late lunch or early dinner. It was decorated with various things related to Philadelphia. When I saw the sign in English, which is commonly seen in the United States, I laughed because the content was humorous and not a real sign.

When I entered the small shop, there was only one customer, and I asked a male clerk with a hip-hop vibe for the most basic item on the menu, an 8-inch cheesesteak.

While waiting, I looked around the store and saw that all the seasonings were from famous brands, so I was looking forward to it because it felt like a store with some pride, just like the last Happy Burger Day in Yeonnam-dong.

Gradually, more customers came in, and by the time the place was quite full, another customer and I were sharing the cheesesteaks we ordered.

At first glance, the cheesesteak was of a reasonable size, but it came with one pickle and one yellow pepper pickle, which I was almost certain was not a dill pickle but a sweet pickle served in this American-style restaurant.

I grabbed the cheesesteak made with soft sandwich bread that was made to order, and it was freshly cooked and hot enough. I bit into it carefully to avoid burning the roof of my mouth, and it was good because it had the thick texture of beef and cheese that I expected.

As I ate it, it wasn't just hot, but also had a subtle spiciness. I could see pieces of jalapenos, so it felt like it was for Koreans who easily feel greasy, but it wasn't overly spicy so it didn't bother me, and it also contained chopped onions.

The cheese seemed to contain provolone cheese or American Swiss cheese, not Cheese Whiz or American cheese, so I inquired and they said it contained American Swiss cheese. I looked somewhere and saw that there was a store in the local area, so I inquired and they said there were two more.

The pickles were, of course, dill pickles, and I enjoyed them until the end and got up from my seat.

Overall, I stopped by because a store serving Philly cheesesteaks opened in Garosu-gil, and I'm not sure if it's a particularly good restaurant in the U.S., but it recreates the general taste that comes to mind when you think of Philly cheesesteaks, and it's delicious because it has a good amount of volume.

reviews.author: Y.H. Chun
reviews.text:
One-line review: A place where the atmosphere and props account for half of the taste.
(A place that stimulates the nostalgia of people from Philly…)

The owner, who had studied there, told me that it had opened, so I went to visit. Wheel of fortune appears on TV, and goods and bottle beer bring back memories of Philly... It makes old memories pass by like a flash.

The most important cheesesteak…
Most reviews praise it as authentic and real Philly cheesesteak, but…
Personally, the looking is similar, but the taste and quantity... It is difficult to compare it to Geno’s or Pat’s. As expected, the difference in hoagie roll seems to have the biggest impact, followed by the biggest difference in amount. If you are thinking of coming from the US, we recommend ordering as Philly Special (+9,000 won extra).

The taste was a little disappointing, but it was still nice to be able to reminisce about my young Philly college days in Seoul thanks to the owner's challenge to open a restaurant like this. May you prosper… .

[In response to the president’s reply on February 12, 2023]

Thank you for your kind reply. ^^ Is there anyone who has lived in Philly without their own favorite cheesesteak place? ^^(I also lived in Philly for about 10 years, and my favorite cheesesteak place was a small store in the neighborhood...) I mentioned two places because they are the most famous and because they were the first to make cheesesteak, I thought that most people would know about them and be able to evaluate what this place feels like compared to other places... .

It's great to see you leave a reply like this and think about progress... I believe that no place can satisfy all customers 100%. The uniqueness of the store that is loved by the public and can be evaluated as ‘intent to visit again’… And the ability to keep it consistent... Of course, it's not easy, but I think that's what the best and long-running stores have in common.  Next time, we look forward to seeing the charming cheesesteaks unique to this place that are more satisfying as you put in more effort.

thank you

reviews.author: ANNEZUE
reviews.text:
I had lunch here. It was the worst restaurant among Michelin 2-star fine dining restaurants. The service was not good.
I visited to celebrate my birthday, and they said I couldn't eat the cake, so I left it in the car.
I ordered a glass of chamomile yuzu sparkling non-alcoholic wine and Coke Zero.
The first dish was an amuse bouche of three one-bite dishes. The dish called Hoedeopbap was made with taco chips made from seaweed and used perilla salad and horseradish custard to give it a rice-like texture. Green mustard leaves were added to add a spicy kick, and topped with seasonal scallop scallops and Japanese pepper powder. Next, they explained a dish called Chodang Corn, which turned out to be the food description at the end. I thought he would first explain what was right next to it, but he introduced me to the raw rice bowl on the front right and explained Chodang Corn at the very back. I think the service is really lacking in this area. Chodang Corn is a crispy potato chip filled with apple mint and lime zest in the style of a Cobb salad, and the Chodang Corn, corn puree, and herbs were placed on top to make it look like a flower pot. The last one was a food called scorched rice, fermented rice. The inside of the nurungji chips made using rice dough was filled with charcoal-grilled raw meat, black garlic, and Cheonhyeong, and the top was finished with mayonnaise and nutritious chives. The raw fish rice bowl had a sour taste, and the salad tasted like rice, just as described. The scallops on top had a soft texture without a chewy texture. The tacos were crispy and thin, so they fell apart easily. The chodang corn was delicious and harmonious with the sweet taste of corn kernels and the crumbly cup made from potatoes. The scorched rice was the most delicious of the courses. It was unusual because it was soggy and not crispy, and the raw meat was chewy and delicious. The mayonnaise sauce was rich.

The second dish was water parsley kimchi. Water parsley stems were wrapped around horse mackerel sashimi to add flavor, and sliced radish, tangerine powder, and red pepper were used on top to add a crunchy texture. Refreshing juice said to be made from Jeju tangerines was poured, and Cheongyang pepper oil, which had a spicy and refreshing taste, was added. The sweet and sour spicy broth and the crunchiness of the radish were impressive and went well with the chewy texture of the horse mackerel.

The third dish was fried asparagus. The fried food surrounding the asparagus was fried tofu skin called yuba. They said they mixed spicy tomatoes, paprika, and zucchini with nut paste to add flavor. They said there was tomato powder and various herbs on top, but it was just fried asparagus. It was warm, crunchy, and delicious. The fried yuba was sour. It was just that. It wasn't delicious, but it wasn't so bad that I couldn't eat it.

The fourth dish was an additional snail dish. It was a dish with egg custard, truffle oil, green onion oil, pan-fried snail spinach, and parmesan cheese on top. It tasted like salty parmesan cheese and steamed eggs. The snails were chewy, but with the steamed egg, it was like a snail. It had a subtle spinach scent. It's ridiculous to say that this is the representative menu, and it was disappointing. It was really bad.

The fifth dish was a pancake and croaker dish. The croaker was boiled, and broccoli, zucchini, and green beans were mixed with black vinegar and maple syrup to add flavor. Fresh lemon gel, sarangcho, and potato chips were added on top, and finally, pancha sauce was poured. In a teacup, croaker broth with spices such as kaffir lime oil and juniper berries was served. The croaker broth was more delicious than the food. The soft flesh of the croaker and the fresh lime seemed like some vague Southeast Asian food, but I didn't like it. I only liked the texture of the potato chips. I was so disappointed. I think it would taste better if I made it at home.The sixth dish was dumplings made in the shape of abalone. Abalones were aged in kelp to give them a chewy and soft texture. Dumplings with blackcurrant mushrooms in a paste made of green onions and a sauce made from seaweed were served. The dumplings were delicious and the seaweed sauce was delicious. The umami was creamy, like an ink sauce.

The seventh dish was Korean beef tenderloin. They quickly grilled it on a camping charcoal called binchotan and gently prepared it through resting. There were 3 side dishes. When preparing the 3 side dishes, the server introduced the left and right foods. For the guests, the oxtail ssamjang was on the far right, and the server explained that he would start with the food on the left, but it turned out that the food on the left and right were switched, so I misunderstood. I listened carefully to what kind of food it was. There was confusion in the process. The basic service is to explain the food left and right based on the customer, not the server, but this was a service where the customer had to endure the inconvenience. The explanation was also quickly told and left. The ssamjang was oxtail meat mixed in spicy soybean paste sauce and topped with various nuts. It was really delicious. If it was sold, I wanted to buy it in bulk and eat it at home. The next side dish was seasoned whelk. They said it was seasoned with chive aioli sauce, topped with anchovy seasoning and reddish, and served with salted fish. The third side dish I was confused about was cucumber sobagi made with oil fermented in paprika sauce. The meat was cooked medium rare and the taste of the meat was just the same. The oxtail ssamjang tasted great. It had oxtail, soybean paste, red pepper, and garlic. The ssamjang with the nutty taste of pecans on top was extremely delicious. The whelk, chive and anchovy sauce was also good to eat with the meat. The whelk seasoned was chewy and the cucumber cabbage was just so-so.

The eighth dish was maple and cheddar ice cream. The ice cream had a rich flavor using aged maple syrup, and on the bottom, it had cheddar cheese sauce and brioche and quinoa puffs made from pumpkin seeds to add a crunchy texture, and it was finished with dried onion powder on top. It was delicious. It was sweet and salty, and the texture of the pumpkin brioche and quinoa puffs was the best. It popped in my mouth.

Ninth, there were three kinds of kkoduram. He told me that it means the last in pure Korean. He also said that the peach and sand cookie called Cheonjungdo had parmesan cheese cream and basil ganache in between. The minjimak was served with green apple and cardamom jelly. Cheonjungdo peach was moderately sweet and not high in sugar. I wonder why this came out.
The black tea had a nice cocoa scent and was sold separately, but it would have been nice if they had also sold oxtail ssamjang instead of this.
The cardamom jelly tasted like convenience store pudding jelly. It had a chewy texture with raw sugar on the outside.
The sandwich had an impressive basil-flavored ganache in it. It was unique and seemed like a combination of a dessert and a meal.

Overall, I was very disappointed with the taste and service. The tables were close together and there was a tablet on the table, so it was like a local kalguksu restaurant. I would visit again if it tasted good, but it was the most unsatisfactory place I've ever been to.

reviews.author: ANNEZUE
reviews.text:
Even though I arrived first, I wasn't assigned a window seat and had to sit near the kitchen door. Usually, a staff member greets you at the entrance, but here, names were checked inside the kitchen, and it was also inconvenient to have to wait for late guests. It was disappointing that the food was served first to those who came late. There were no drinks such as cola or cider, so I ordered kombucha and house wine, and also ordered onion soup as an additional menu item.
The first dish was a tomato dish. Tomatoes were marinated in homemade sauce for two days, and under the tomatoes, they made a jam-like drink by boiling onions, cherry vinegar, honey, and port wine. They then put fermented yogurt sauce on top of the tomatoes. They said they made foam with the whey that forms during the yogurt making process. There were walnut crumbles sprinkled around it.
It wasn't as sour as I thought, and the yogurt cream on top was sweet. The herbal scent lingered at the end to whet my appetite, and the taste exceeded my expectations.
The abalone dish was prepared by gently boiling it at low temperature for 2 hours, and the white sauce was an aioli sauce made with garlic and egg yolk. The black salad under the abalone was a sour salad made with lentils, couscous, quinoa, and onions, and the top of the abalone was a dish with abalone intestine sauce and potato crumbles. The abalone was chewy and went well with the crumble, giving it a variety of textures. However, the sauce tasted like a mixture of light mayonnaise and lemon, and the overall acidity was strong, which was disappointing.
He said that the cod dish should be cooked lightly with potato puree, seasonal vegetables, cod brought from Garak Market, and white wine, and eaten with the carrot puree and potato puree on the bottom. Overall, it was a dish that left a heavy taste in the mouth, and the cod meat was soft, and the tomato that came with it was especially delicious.
The mushroom dish was made with black barley instead of regular rice, so it had a nice popping texture, and the flavor was even richer with pecorino cheese. On top were oyster mushrooms that were grilled in olive oil and over a high heat until crispy. On the bottom, button mushrooms were thinly sliced and added with onion, garlic, butter, and lemon juice to create a sour dish. The dish was finished with parsley, truffle oil, and pepper. It had a subtle truffle scent and was moist. The mushrooms and chewy black barley went well together. Onion soup was served as an additional menu item. The soup was made using organic onions, boiled neatly in vegetable stock, and topped with homemade baguette and herbs such as dill and thyme. The soup was thin, clear, hot, and seasoned just right.
The dessert (Seoritae bean pudding & pineapple sorbet) was said to be a vegan dessert. The pudding was topped with Seoritae crumble and the herb thyme, and the pineapple sorbet was finished with lime zest. The Seoritae soybean pudding was really delicious, and it was the best pudding I've ever had. It was a taste that I wanted to buy in bulk and stock up on at home. The pineapple sorbet was nice to finish off neatly.  In fact, the course was ordinary and there were no dishes that impressed me. Instead, the dessert was so satisfying that I couldn't stop thinking about it.

reviews.text:
The food itself was okay and the portions were quite large, but unfortunately I don't want to go to this restaurant again. I was disappointed from the moment I arrived. There was a very unpleasant smell coming from the entrance, probably due to trash that had not been removed. My first impression was absolutely terrible. No matter how delicious the food is, a smelly entrance makes the entire restaurant feel poorly maintained and dirty.
Even though I made a reservation, I ended up sitting at a table in the corner near the kitchen, even though there were many empty tables in better places. It felt careless and inconsiderate, as if the staff had no regard for the guests' tastes. Additionally, there was a large open window onto the terrace, which looked nice at first but soon became a problem. There were several bugs flying around throughout the meal. I ended up having to kill two mosquitoes and a fly, and another one kept hovering near my plate. It was really unpleasant to eat while constantly distracted by insects.
Service was also disappointing. When we sat down, the staff just handed us the menu without saying anything. There was no greeting, no description of the food, or any recommendations. Everything seemed rushed and impersonal. The food came out very quickly after ordering, which may sound good at first, but it actually added to the impression that the atmosphere was more mechanical than welcoming. Chopsticks were thrown haphazardly on the table, showing no kindness or attention to detail.
I admit that the portions were generous and the food tasted good, but the food wasn't satisfying enough to make me want to come back again. The unpleasant smell, bug problem, uncomfortable seating, and indifferent service completely overshadowed this restaurant's strengths. Eating out should be comfortable and enjoyable, but this experience was stressful and disappointing.
Overall, the food tasted good, but the surroundings made eating uncomfortable. Large portions cannot make up for poor ambiance and poor service. Unfortunately, this place completely ruined what was supposed to be a simple, comfortable dinner.

It's been a long time since I visited here to go on a date with my husband.

★Interior★
Totally Nordic style. It seems like you paid close attention to every detail.
This is an interior you’ll often see when you go to Copenhagen. Everything from the semi-basement restaurant to the terrace is Scandinavian-style. LOL

★Recommended food★
Be sure to try the tea. It was very delicious. (see photo)
What I remember most is that most of the food was delicious, especially because they used a lot of ingredients that are not easy to find in Korea. Rhubarb, leeks, etc.
So I was surprised. You may think the menu is expensive, but the ingredients themselves are all expensive. ㅠㅠ...!

There is no place in Korea that makes proper Danish food, but if you want to try it, I recommend you visit.

★Service★
The service was so good~! All staff were friendly,
He had good manners. What I especially remember is that he ordered a drink and waited to be served because he thought he was eating it with food. A truly European feeling..! Totally impressed.
I really praise this part~ haha

And the menu itself is unfamiliar to Koreans, so there are some menu items that only Danish people would know about, so please explain them one by one, despite your busy schedule. moved.

★What was not good★
If it wasn't the terrace, it was too noisy because there were a lot of people.
Normally, I would read a book while having a cup of coffee... but there were so many people that it was noisy... haha... that's a shame. This can't be helped...
I guess I should visit on a weekday next time.

★Tip★
There doesn't seem to be any room if you want to visit after 12pm.
I think you should make a reservation in advance and visit on the weekend.
It doesn't seem like a good place to visit with children. (Oh, it doesn’t matter if you sit on the terrace with your kids)

It has an atmosphere that makes it better to visit with friends rather than on a date.
I'm not sure about the evening, but there were more people visiting with friends during the day~ (when I visited) ^^!

100% intention to visit again. I will visit again next time!

reviews.text:
Ananti at Gangnam is a hotel opened in Gangnam in 2022 by Ananti, a Korean hotel brand.
Ananti at Gangnam was also designed by architect Min Seong-jin of SKM Design Office, who has always been in charge of Ananti's projects.

On this visit, we visited Beckett, a brunch restaurant on the first floor.
The menu consists of 6 toasts, and the beverage menu has a diverse assortment including coffee, tea, and ade.
I ordered the first menu, smoked salmon and ratatouille toast.
It is an open sandwich style with various ingredients on top of toasted bread.
Ratatouille was on top of the bread like sauce, and on top of it were smoked salmon, boiled eggs, and tartar sauce.
A combination that looks delicious just by listing it.
I like the pickles that come with it because they are not spicy and have a fresh feel.
The coffee included in the set menu is closer to the savory type rather than the sour type and is quite strong.

For dessert, I additionally ordered bread and mango shaved ice.
The mango shaved ice has white cubes in it. Thinking about the nationally famous shaved ice chain, is it cheese? I thought it was a rusk with a hint of garlic or onion.
Maybe it's a unique point of its own.

As it is a hotel facility, the price range is quite high, but I was indebted to it for a friend's wedding invitation party.
Although it is Gangnam, it is not crowded, so I was able to spend time leisurely.
A place I would like to choose as a meeting place that requires personal attention.
I had a good time.

I was a little worried because it was vegan fine dining, but I enjoyed it very much. All four adult men said they were full, so there is no need to worry about this.

The course is quite long, so it takes a while to eat, so if you have a future schedule, you should consider this. It was very good from start to finish and dessert, and it was amazing that it was possible to have a full meal without meat. Usually, they explain each menu well, but because we went as a group, they only served 2-3 of the menu items and skipped the explanation. A bit disappointing.

The size of the restaurant is smaller than expected, so a total of 17 people including the bar table? We were able to get about 4 people, and there are about 2 seats for 4 people, but it seems likely that 2 people will be seated at the bar table with other guests, so keep that in mind.

Wine pairing is also available, but we did not use it since we visited during the day. If you're visiting in the evening, the pairing seems really good. The food itself was so good that I was satisfied.

Another thing worth noting is that you definitely get hungry quickly, so we were full at the time of the meal, but by the time we went home, everyone was hungry and ate ramen. Rather than going there just to feel full, I think it's a great restaurant if you go there with the feeling, "Oh, there's a place like this."

They explained the food well every time it came out, and the plating was so pretty. The herbs and flowers as garnishes were so cute. The sauce that came with the food went well with it and was delicious, but it was also fun to see the colorful colors of the food!! I came alone today, but next time I want to come with friends and family. Cutlets are not included in the course and are ordered as an additional menu item. reviews.author: Tim Jai Sweety
reviews.text:
Last moment before boarding! The week-long journey was neither short nor long, but it passed in the blink of an eye.

Even though I stayed in Sinsa, which has convenient transportation and many shops on the street, I only had time to look around the neighborhood right before departure.

Since I was running out of time, I ate lunch quickly and went back to the KYVE cafe I had passed by earlier and bought some pancakes from the display.

If it weren't for the corner full of cosmetics and clothes, I wouldn't have known that this cafe was run by the vegan cosmetics brand KCOSland.

I ordered creme brûlée at Sinsa Cafe. I was debating between a latte and the seasonal chestnut milk coffee, and chose the crème brûlée coffee based on the staff's recommendation. The thin, crispy sugar crust was lightly caramelized and baked to perfection, and a light tap revealed a creamy custard cream. The vanilla seeds gently seep in and the sweet scent spreads softly and gently like milk foam, creating a perfect harmony with the flavor of milk coffee. The subtle caramel flavor neutralized the strong taste.

Don't underestimate the large Brick Lane scones. It's really generous with lots of cream cheese! The scone itself was crispy on the outside and fluffy on the inside, so it wasn't too dry, and even though it was filled with plenty of cream cheese, it wasn't soggy. White sesame seeds are sprinkled to add flavor, and a little sugar is sprinkled to give it a sweet taste like honey. When I took a bite, it was more delicious than I expected, combining the subtle cheese flavor and the unique oily taste of a savory scone.
But unfortunately, I didn't realize that the drink I chose was quite sweet and I added too much sugar to the scone, so it ended up feeling a bit greasy at the end...
